title: Present value from tables
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank points either work out present value by summing discounted payments or cover tables of both future and present value factors, so neither matches this narrower table-only present value idea.

draft.title: Present value from tables
card: The present value of an annuity is the single amount that, invested now, would grow to the same total as the annuity. It is a lump sum today that matches the regular payments.
Present value = payment × present value factor. The factor comes from a table, found using the interest rate per period and the number of periods.
Rate per period = annual rate ÷ periods per year. Number of periods = years × periods per year. Example: 6% p.a. paid monthly for 2 years is 0.5% per month for 24 periods.
Worked example: $1000 paid each year for 3 years at 2% p.a. The table factor is 2.8839. Present value = 1000 × 2.8839 = $2883.90.
draft.remember: Present value = payment × table factor, using the rate and periods for each payment.

a.q: An annuity pays $2000 each year for 5 years at 2% p.a. The table factor for 2% and 5 periods is 4.7135. What is its present value?
a.why: Present value = 2000 × 4.7135 = $9427.00. Dividing by the factor gives $424.31, which reverses the method. The factor is multiplied by the payment.
a.clue: The payment and the factor are combined by one operation.

b.q: Mia wants the lump sum today that matches $300 paid each month for 3 years at 6% p.a. compounded monthly. Which table factor does she need?
b.why: Payments are monthly, so the rate is 6% ÷ 12 = 0.5% per month and the periods are 3 × 12 = 36. Using 6% and 3 periods uses the annual figures, which do not match monthly payments.
b.clue: Both the rate and the number of periods must match how often payments are made.

check.summary: No problems found. The table factors (2.8839 and 4.7135), the worked example and both answers all check out.
